verdict.rationale: Docs show building blocks — transactional webhooks track spam, unsub, hard-bounce, reject events (docs-18) and a rejection allowlist/denylist system (docs-17) — implying suppression logic exists, and community reports (comm-5, comm-6) confirm spam complaints trigger account-level suppression/blocking of sends. However, there is no explicit first-party documentation stating that unsubscribes/bounces/complaints are automatically suppressed and honored uniformly across every send type (campaigns, automations, transactional, SMS), and some community accounts describe suppression behavior as opaque or overly blunt rather than a clean compliance guarantee. missing for 10: explicit doc on automatic suppression-list enforcement across all send types, independent deliverability audit confirming CAN-SPAM/GDPR default compliance.
